extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO enrollment & discipline staff, and legal professionals interested in USPTO reciprocal-discipline procedures
extracted.subtask_description: A final USPTO order imposing reciprocal discipline (exclusion) under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on a State Bar revocation for ethical violations, and specifying procedural, publication, and reinstatement obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for exclusion under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion from practice before the USPTO may be ordered pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 when reciprocal discipline is sought based on a practitioner's disciplinary sanction imposed by a State authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director considers whether there is a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d). If no genuine issue exists, the Director may impose discipline identical to that imposed by the State (here, exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) when the practitioner's license to practice law in a State is revoked on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of that State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a federal regulation violation can serve as the basis for reciprocal discipline by the USPTO when the State revocation is on ethical grounds (as in the cited Virginia State Bar action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to act with reasonable diligence and promptness (Virginia RPC 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Admitted violation of Virginia Rule of Professional Conduct 1.3 by failing to act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client and by intentionally failing to carry out a contract of employment entered into with a client for professional services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites this as one of the ethical bases underlying the State revocation that supports reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to keep client reasonably informed and respond to requests (Virginia RPC 1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Admitted violation of Virginia Rule of Professional Conduct 1.4 by failing to keep a client reasonably informed about the status of a matter and failing to promptly comply with reasonable requests for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of communication with a client is treated as a professional-conduct violation contributing to reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to safekeep property and maintain records (Virginia RPC 1.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Admitted violation of Virginia Rule of Professional Conduct 1.15 for failing to properly safekeep property and maintain records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper handling or recordkeeping of client property is a serious ethical failing cited in the State decision and relied upon by the USPTO in imposing exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure upon termination to protect client's interest and return property (Virginia RPC 1.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Admitted violation of Virginia Rule of Professional Conduct 1.16 by failing upon termination of services to reasonably protect a client's interest and to return property of the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to protect client interests at termination is an independent ground cited for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond to a lawful demand for information from a disciplinary authority (Virginia RPC 8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Admitted violation of Virginia Rule of Professional Conduct 8.1 by failing to respond to a lawful demand for information from a disciplinary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncooperation with disciplinary investigations is a basis for reciprocal disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Order service and response requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice and Order informs the respondent of the Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline and directs that, to contest imposition of identical discipline, the respondent must file a response within 40 days containing all information believed sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file such a response (or inability to receive the mailing) can lead the Director to determine that no genuine issue of material fact exists and to impose reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication and alternative service methods (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24(b), 11.35(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: When mailed notices are returned unclaimed and unable to be forwarded, the USPTO may effect service by publication (e.g., in the Official Gazette) as authorized by 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24(b) and 11.35(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service by publication notifies the respondent of the proceeding and availability of documents (e.g., Notice and Order) via requests to the USPTO General Counsel; it supports proceeding when direct service fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for Director's determination under § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director must determine whether (1) there is a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and (2) whether imposition of identical discipline is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no genuine issue of material fact exists and identical discipline is appropriate, the Director may impose the same discipline as the State (here, exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance obligations during exclusion (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner excluded from practice must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order grants a limited recognition period to facilitate compliance with § 11.58(b) and explicitly requires adherence to the regulations governing excluded practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to facilitate compliance (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order grants the respondent limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date the Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after that date for the sole purpose of facilitating compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This narrow, time-limited recognition is provided only to allow the respondent to comply with obligations (e.g., client notice/transfer) required by the exclusion rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette and, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, give notice of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication and notice ensure public transparency and inform other jurisdictions and courts about the practitioner's exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent seeking reinstatement after exclusion must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly conditions any future reinstatement request on adherence to the regulatory reinstatement standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority cited (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32)
rubrics_metrics.description: The action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, which provide statutory authority for the USPTO's disciplinary procedures and actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing the statutory basis identifies the legal authority underpinning the USPTO's reciprocal discipline processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to disciplinary decisions (OED Reading Room posting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room (OED Reading Room) accessible via the USPTO website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting decisions provides notice to the public and interested parties and documents the basis for disciplinary actions.
